diagnosis: Small cell carcinoma of the lung
legend: FNAC. A dirty background containing clusters of cells with scant cytoplasm and overlapping nuclei with moulding and dispersed chromatin. Nucleoli are inconspicuous.

diagnosis: Small cell carcinoma of the lung
legend: Core biopsy. Sheets of small cells showing discohesive pattern in a fibrotic stromal background. Nuclei are irregular, with finely granular chromatin and no evident nucleoli.

diagnosis: Small cell carcinoma of the lung
legend: Ki-67 (MIB1) immunohistochemistry on a core biopsy. Necrosis may be absent and mitotic figures may be difficult to evaluate in biopsy samples. Ki-67 (MIB1) staining may be very helpful to sustain a diagnosis of small cell carcinoma in this setting, such as in the present case with a high (albeit heterogeneous) proliferation rate (exceeding 70%).

Tumour cells are densely packed in a discohesive pattern with a poor stroma component. Nuclear chromatin is finely dispersed or has a salt-and-pepper appearance. Small nucleoli are present in only very few cells.
Neoplastic cells show diffuse and intense cytoplasmic positivity for synaptophysin.
Neoplastic cells show diffuse nuclear positivity for INSM1, although with heterogeneous intensity.
A malignant neoplasm infiltrating the bladder wall made of spindling small cells in a solid growth pattern intersected by rare fibrotic bands.
Neoplastic cells show a heterogeneous pattern of cytoplasmic positivity for synaptophysin.
The Ki-67 index in neoplastic cells is homogeneously high (> 70% in this example).
